title: Faster dnasp compute_k on the rp49 sliding windows
workload: Ingroup of skills/dnasp/tests/fixtures/inputs/rp49_ing34_outGUA.fas with outgroup rp49.gua removed. Window 100 bp, step 25 bp, same loop as run_analysis. complete_deletion runs before the timer; compute_k is called on each of the 69 non-empty windows, which is what analyse_region does.
result_constraint: The 69 compute_k floats stay bit-identical. The harness checksum is sha256 over their little-endian float64 bytes, in window order.
notes: Different function from the merged compute_ka_ks change in ClawBio/ClawBio#734. No open PR touches compute_k. Seven fresh processes after one warmup; the checksum was the same on every run. A scratch NumPy Hamming count on these same prepared windows returned that checksum. Its in-process median over 7 repeats was 6.50 ms, spread 4.23%.

title: Faster genome-compare parse of the Church 23andMe file
workload: One call on skills/genome-compare/data/george_church_23andme.txt.gz (569279 SNPs), the reference file the skill's tests parse.
result_constraint: The returned genotype dict and position dict stay equal. The harness checksum sorts rsids, so dict order does not affect it.
notes: The call builds a GenotypeRecord per SNP and then copies that into the two dicts the skill keeps. A scratch one-pass build of those two dicts compared equal to the current return value and matched this checksum. Five in-process calls had median 0.739 s (samples 0.780, 0.745, 0.727, 0.739, 0.728). That sits below every baseline sample. Gzip read of the same file is about 0.12 s, so the time is the Python objects.

title: Lower peak memory while parsing the Church 23andMe file
workload: tracemalloc peak of one call on skills/genome-compare/data/george_church_23andme.txt.gz. Tracing starts after imports. The checksum runs after tracing stops.
result_constraint: The returned genotype dict and position dict stay equal. Same checksum as the wall-time harness.
notes: Peak is tracemalloc's peak traced bytes, not RSS. All seven processes reported 288356128. The scratch one-pass parse that matched the checksum peaked at 213908239, 213921839, and 213908095 bytes under the same tracing. The retained genotype and position dicts are the result; the extra peak is the GenotypeRecord map that the function discards.
